label: Learjet 60 N722BD is flying from Austin to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, with nine people on board. It nears Fort Myers at 41,000 ft. Heavy rain lies ahead over south Florida.
Miami Center warns of moderate to extreme precipitation ahead, about 100 miles across. The crew will fly via FIMED, then Freeport.
The crew turn left of course around the weather. The heights on screen are true altitude: in the warm air FL350 is near 37,000 ft.
The route skirts the large storm area to the north-west. On the radar the track stays in moderate rain, about 35 to 45 dBZ, not in the red core.
Learjet 60 N722BD is on its way from Austin to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, with nine people on board. It is crossing south Florida at FL350, in thunderstorms.

Turning direct Freeport, the crew report light clear ice and moderate turbulence. The pilot says "plus or minus... 700 feet, 600 feet". The ADS-B shows the climb rate swinging by about that many feet per minute, and height by under 100 ft. Outside air temperature: −47 °C.
The turn direct to Freeport swings the track from north-east to east, toward a single storm cell west of West Palm Beach. On the radar its core is over 50 dBZ.
The crew report precipitation as the aircraft reaches the cell, where the radar shows 46 to 57 dBZ on its track. They ask for FL370, and it is already climbing at about 1,300 ft/min.
Top of the climb: 35,450 ft pressure altitude
The climb ends inside the cell, about 450 ft above where it began, as the crew finish reading back FL370. Within seconds the aircraft is going down.
About 15 seconds after the top of the climb the descent rate passes 10,000 ft a minute, and the crew call mayday. The aircraft then turns right as it falls.
The broadcast rate stops at its 32,640 ft/min limit. The aircraft's GNSS height shows more than 50,000 ft/min in the last seconds. What part ice or the storm played is not known.
Crash site: Military Trail at 10th Avenue North
